data.title: Hypoinsulinaemia, glucose intolerance and diminished beta-cell size in S6K1-deficient mice
data.authors: Pende M; Kozma SC; Jaquet M; Oorschot V; Burcelin R; Le Marchand-Brustel Y; Klumperman J; Thorens B; Thomas G

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: S6K1 knockout mice; isolated muscle insulin sensitivity; pancreatic islet morphometry and insulin secretion
data.finding: Mice lacking S6 kinase 1 had low blood insulin and were glucose intolerant. Isolated muscle from these mice did not show insulin resistance; instead, glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and pancreatic insulin content were sharply reduced. Glucose sensing and insulin production per se were intact: the defect was a smaller pancreatic endocrine mass, explained by a selective decrease in beta-cell size. The authors noted that the phenotype resembles preclinical type 2 diabetes in which poor nutrition early in life leads to low insulin. Boundary: Mouse genetic knockout with lifelong S6K1 loss. Not tested in people. Drafted from the abstract only.
data.abstract_excerpt: Insulin controls glucose homeostasis by regulating glucose use in peripheral tissues, and its own production and secretion in pancreatic beta cells. These responses are largely mediated downstream of the insulin receptor substrates, IRS-1 and IRS-2 (refs 4-8), through distinct signalling pathways. Although a number of effectors of these pathways have been identified, their roles in mediating glucose homeostasis are poorly defined.

extracted_findings.target: Beta-cell size, insulin secretion, glucose tolerance
extracted_findings.effect: Loss of S6K1 reduces beta-cell size and insulin output, causing glucose intolerance
